messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dp-valentech-prod' is reporting GPU node exhaustion. 95% queue depth for tenant ValenTech. Paging oncall-mike :rotating_light:

oncall-mike: I’m on it. Pulling metrics now.

sara_sre: I see elevated allocation for valentech-tenantID=val123, spikes started ~10:02 UTC. GPU utilization 99% on pool nodes g4-24.

raj_infra: Confirming autoscaler didn't kick. Scaling policy for dp-valentech-prod has hard cap = 8 nodes, current nodes = 8.

oncall-mike: Reproducing:
```
rictl pools describe dp-valentech-prod --json | jq '.nodes | length'
# returns 8
rictl pools metrics dp-valentech-prod --range 5m --metric gpu_util | tail -n 1
# 99.2%
```

oncall-mike: This is a single-tenant dedicated pool hitting its max nodes. Customer requests are queuing and getting 429 throttles. Need decision: allow burst to shared spare capacity or throttle/queue.

jess_cs: Customer success (jess_cs) here. ValenTech is in a paid enterprise contract with 99.95% latency SLA for inference. They are on-call too. @kevin_prod can confirm how bad customer is seeing it.

kevin_prod: ValenTech engineering reported ~20% of calls failing with timeouts from their side, some 500s returned from our edge. Impacting their live feature. They asked for immediate mitigation.

nora_ops: Quick ask: do we have spare burst capacity in region-us-west2?

raj_infra: There are 3 nodes in the shared-burst-pool-us-west2 but they are currently reserved for high-priority fallback. Policy allows manual temporary attach for P1 incidents with documented CS approval.

oncall-mike: Proposal: attach shared-burst-pool-us-west2 to dp-valentech-prod for 30m to drain queue, then detach. Will need ops + CS signoff. Command would be:
```
rictl pools attach-shared dp-valentech-prod --shared shared-burst-pool-us-west2 --duration 30m --reason "emergency customer burst"
```

jess_cs: ValenTech approves temporary burst. They asked we notify when done. +1 from CS.

sara_sre: Security check: no customer data will leave their dedicated pool; shared nodes will still be isolated at tenant level via runtime namespaces. I’ll run quick verification.

raj_infra: If we attach shared nodes, we must enable tenant isolation on the added nodes. I'll prepare commands.

nora_ops: I will perform the attach once infra confirms isolation config. Please post commands.

raj_infra: Running isolation configuration snippet now:
```
rictl node configure --node shared-node-3 --tenant val123 --isolation=namespace --apply
rictl node status shared-node-3
# status: isolated -> OK
```

deploy-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: isolation-config v1.2 -> shared-node-3 (triggered by raj_infra)

raj_infra: Attach command prepared.

nora_ops: Executing attach...
```
rictl pools attach-shared dp-valentech-prod --shared shared-burst-pool-us-west2 --duration 30m --reason "emergency customer burst"
```

nora_ops: Attach complete. New node count = 11. Queue length dropping.

oncall-mike: Observability: queue depth down from 95% -> 20% in 4 minutes. Token cost and latency metrics look back to normal for now.

kevin_prod: Customer confirms degraded traffic is recovering. They are monitoring.

sara_sre: Running post-action checks: verifying KV cache warmup and model kernels on new nodes. Some cold start latencies initially ~300ms for first few requests, expected.

oncall-mike: Will keep the burst for 30m unless we decide earlier. Leaving this thread open for handoff.

jess_cs: I’ve informed ValenTech account team and support. They requested incident reference. I’ll collect timeline for post-incident summary.

nora_ops: 30m window started at 10:12 UTC. Scheduled detach at 10:42 UTC. Setting reminder.

sara_sre: Note: autoscaler cap of 8 is intentional due to cost controls on dedicated pools. We should follow up with product about whether to relax cap for valentech.

oncall-mike: Handing off to sara_sre for follow-up post-burst. I need to go to a different pager.

sara_sre: Acknowledged. Will monitor until detach. @raj_infra can you prepare rollback plan in case detach causes re-queue?

raj_infra: Rollback plan: on detach, if queue > 30% then automatically re-route traffic to host fallback models (lower-cost variant) and open a fast rollback attach. Command:
```
rictl pools detach-shared dp-valentech-prod --shared shared-burst-pool-us-west2 || rictl traffic redirect --tenant val123 --model fallback-small
```

nora_ops: Detach started at 10:41:50 UTC.

deploy-bot: DETACH RUN: pools.detach initiated for shared-burst-pool-us-west2 -> dp-valentech-prod

nora_ops: Detach complete at 10:42:10 UTC. Node count back to 8. Queue stable at 12%. 429s gone.

kevin_prod: Customer confirms normal operations. They appreciate the quick support.

jess_cs: ValenTech wants a post-incident review and to discuss increasing pool cap for off-peak burst. Scheduling meeting.

sara_sre: I’ll own the incident writeup. Captured timeline and config commands. Next steps: (1) review autoscaler caps and cost guardrails for enterprise dedicated pools, (2) add an automation to attach shared-burst for P1 with CS approval, (3) improve alert to include "near-cap" warnings earlier.

oncall-mike: Thanks team. Marking this thread resolved for active mitigation. Please add any follow-ups here. :white_check_mark:
